answer: Pay data agents by marginal contribution, not headcount. When reports on, say, a canyon trail's flood risk arrive, the protocol scores each one leave-one-out: how far the final estimate moves if that report is dropped. A hundred clones echoing one sensor add almost nothing past the first, so they split a single reward while each still pays a filing fee. Only an independent observer, like a ranger who saw the willow roots wash out, adds real signal. The math makes it crystal clear: copying earns nothing.
